failure_analysis.primary_failure: A short completed flow reversal after a common spot-perpetual external sweep and reclaim was not durable evidence of auction rotation. Six of seven central trades resumed the original shock direction or invalidated immediately.
failure_analysis.largest_performance_driver: The ACTIVE_FLOW_REVERSAL branch created every central trade and every material loss. The PERSISTENT_FLOW_ABSORPTION branch created no trade at any adjacent accepted-range horizon.
failure_analysis.frequency: The 30m and 60m portfolios had day-trading frequency, but it came entirely from the losing active-reversal branch. The only approximately breakeven 15m result had insufficient frequency and only 0.03% daily growth.
failure_analysis.reward_geometry: Changing accepted-range horizon altered target geometry but did not change the sign of expectancy; central and long horizons remained deeply negative. The root problem was state direction, not target distance.
failure_analysis.why_no_more_parameter_search: The one permitted core-state ablation removed all opportunities across 15m, 30m and 60m. The surviving state is too rare, while the active state is decisively negative. Further threshold tuning would fit noise around a falsified state machine.

valid_components.component: frozen external auction boundary before event
valid_components.why_useful: It gives a causal liquidity location and prevents arbitrary wick classification.
It separates synchronized spot-perpetual events from derivative-only dislocations and improves failure attribution.

valid_components.component: failure retracement and observed sweep-extreme invalidation
valid_components.why_useful: It expresses a coherent failed-auction geometry even though the chosen confirmation did not predict direction.

It produced two wins from four and approximately flat after costs, suggesting short accepted ranges can define useful liquidity objectives after a genuinely valid reversal. It was not frequent or strong enough to retain as a candidate.

next_hypothesis_requirements: Do not infer direction from a common shock or a brief opposite flow average.
Trade a cross-market relative-value gap where the target is observable fair-value convergence rather than a directional forecast of the whole market.
Distinguish spot-led perpetual underreaction from perpetual-only overshoot using pre-event basis and leader-laggard timing.
Require basis convergence to begin before entry and use restored pre-event basis as the natural target.
Keep the event, confirmation and target mechanically distinct, with an ambiguous no-trade state.
Preserve NautilusTrader-only execution, current-NAV 3% risk and sequential unseen-week gates.
